PM Decision Memo

The Command Center is the weekly PM decision layer above the source decks. Current stance is Neutral / selective for equity beta under Selective Only. The tape has enough strength to participate, but the evidence is uneven. Use group and ticker confirmation rather than adding broad exposure. The average z-score overlay is 0.00, so extension/repair is being included in the strategy score rather than treated as a separate afterthought. Risk appetite, financial conditions, drawdown risk, and Options Intelligence set the risk budget; breadth, ETF leadership, and z-scores define the opportunity set; CFTC positioning and VAMS confirm or challenge the exposures.

Leadership: BUG, CRAK, CLOU, KRE Risk watch: URA, URNM, SILJ, GDXJ VAMS overlay: -3.5 Positioning overlay: +4.0 FCI overlay: -2.0 Options overlay: -0.7 Regime: Selective Only

PM workflow: 1) set the risk budget from Risk Appetite, Financial Conditions, S&P 500 Drawdown Safety, and Options Intelligence, 2) pick exposures from breadth, ETF leadership, and z-score repair/extension, 3) confirm with rates/credit, CFTC, Options, and VAMS, then 4) translate the evidence into the allocation model. Strongest group stack is Financial / Health Care Industries, Style / Market Structure, Factors / Risk Appetite; weakest group stack is Growth / Tech Leadership, Thematic / Speculative Growth, Metals / Miners. Price/breadth as of 2026-07-17; breadth metrics as of 2026-07-17; CFTC positioning as of 2026-07-14; VAMS as of 2026-07-22; Options as of 2026-07-16.

Decision Rule

Use the agreement score as the compression layer across the nine live checks: risk appetite, breadth, ETF leadership/z-scores, rates/credit, financial conditions, drawdown risk, Options Intelligence, positioning, and VAMS. It is not a replacement for the evidence.

7-9 checksOwn confirmed risk; avoid only the extended/crowded pockets.
5-6 checksSelective exposure; group confirmation matters more than broad beta.
0-4 checksDefensive posture; wait for breadth, Options, VAMS, FCI, or rates/credit repair.

Conflicts To Resolve

ConflictCurrent ReadPM Resolution
Broad tape vs macro conditionsRisk appetite 46.1 / 100 while FCI is 36.9 / 100.If risk appetite is stronger than FCI, stay invested but prefer confirmed leaders and avoid low-quality chase.
Risk appetite vs drawdown riskRisk appetite 46.1 / 100 while drawdown risk is 54.4 / 100.When both are elevated, stay invested selectively but reduce entry aggressiveness, hedge more deliberately, and favor groups with confirmed breadth/VAMS.
Options pressure vs price leadershipOptions pressure 47.2 / 100 with path risk 44.4, protection demand 50.6, IV pressure 44.3, and leadership call chase 76.4.If options validation says risk control or leadership call chase is high, do not treat price momentum as permission to chase. Require breadth, VAMS, and z-score entry discipline.
Leadership vs entry riskExtended ETFs: n/a; repair watch: none flagged.Add to leaders on pullbacks, not after extension; prioritize repair only when breadth/VAMS confirm.
Momentum vs participationVAMS overlay -3.5; avg damage breadth 21.1%.Fresh VAMS buys matter most when damage is contained; rising damage means size down the signal.
Credit calm vs compensationRates/Credit score 25.97; spreads remain tight.Do not confuse calm with cheap; require stronger breadth before adding lower-quality beta.

Master Risk-Budget Read

The aggregate gauge is the master risk-budget read: 30% Risk Appetite, 30% Financial Conditions, 25% Drawdown Safety, and 15% Options Intelligence. Drawdown Safety is the inverse of drawdown risk. This is the model validation layer. It compares future drawdowns after low-risk readings against future drawdowns after high-risk readings. A useful signal should show deeper average/worst future drawdowns and higher 5%, 10%, and 15% drawdown hit rates in high-risk buckets.

Methodology

This page defines the language used throughout the packet so the weekly read is explainable in a client or investment-committee setting.

Health Score

Composite breadth score from the individual ETF breadth metric files. It answers: are the holdings inside the ETF broadly confirming the price move?

35%Trend Breadth: average % of holdings above 20DMA, 50DMA, and 200DMA
20%Leadership Breadth: average % making new highs or sitting near 52-week highs
15%Positive 20D Return: % of holdings with positive 20-day return
20%Relative Strength: average % outperforming across 30D, 60D, 90D, 6M, and 1Y
-10%Damage Breadth: penalizes new lows and holdings more than 20% below 52-week highs

Weekly Change

Health 1W Change is the 5-trading-day change in the Health Score. This matters because a strong ETF with falling internal health is different from a strong ETF whose internals are still broadening.

ImproverHealth score rising over the last 5 trading days
DeterioratorHealth score falling over the last 5 trading days
ConfirmationPrice return and breadth health moving in the same direction
DivergencePrice return and breadth health moving in opposite directions

Price Proxy Health

For ETFs without constituent breadth files, the packet uses a technical proxy so group summaries are complete instead of blank. The proxy is intentionally less punitive after volatile single-day moves; drawdown damage begins once price is more than 10% below its trailing 1-year high.

45%Trend proxy: above 50DMA, above 200DMA, and positive 1M return
40%Leadership proxy: percentile rank of 1W, 1M, and 3M returns
15%Damage proxy: penalty for drawdown more than 10% below the trailing 1-year high
Health SourceTables mark each row as Breadth or Price proxy

Trend Breadth

Measures whether holdings are above key moving averages. This is the cleanest internal trend confirmation signal.

Above 20DMAShort-term trend participation
Above 50DMAIntermediate trend participation
Above 200DMALong-term trend participation

Damage Breadth

Measures internal stress. High damage breadth means the ETF price can look stable while many constituents remain impaired.

20D New LowsFresh short-term breakdowns
52W New LowsLong-term breakdowns
>20% Below HighDrawdown damage below the ETF surface

ETF Z-Score Overlay

Uses the ETF macro technical deck to judge whether leadership is extended versus each ETF's own history or whether weakness is becoming a repair candidate.

Extension ZAverage of available own-history return z-scores and 50DMA deviation z-score. High positive readings flag chase risk. Negative readings flag washed-out conditions.
MA Dev ZHow far the ETF sits from its moving-average trend versus its own historical behavior.
RS ZRelative-strength z-score versus SPY when available. This is the positive confirmation component.
Repair CandidateExtension Z at or below -0.75 plus either improving 1W breadth health or a positive 1W price return. This flags early repair, not full confirmation.
Z OverlayGroup-level score adjustment: RS z-score bonus minus extension/washout penalties, clipped from -8 to +8, then added to Strategy Score.
Decision UsePositive overlay supports allocation; negative overlay says leadership may be stretched or weakness still needs repair.

How Z-Scores Flow Through

The z-score layer is not just a table. It feeds the group Strategy Score, then flows into the Model Allocation and Allocation Playbook. Cross-Analysis and Regime also show it explicitly as the chase-versus-repair layer.

Cross-AnalysisAdds the question: are we chasing extended winners or buying confirmed repair?
RegimeShows average extension, extended ETF count, washed-out count, and average group z-score overlay.
Model AllocationUses Strategy Score after the z-score overlay is included.
Allocation PlaybookUses the same allocation table, so it stays consistent with the model.

Apex Risk Appetite Gauge

Aggregate 0-100 read built from the same ETF price universe used by the group allocation workflow. It is the broad tape input; the PM allocation tables then add breadth, VAMS, CFTC positioning, Options Intelligence, financial conditions, rates/credit, and z-score overlays.

25%% of ETFs above 50DMA
20%% of ETFs above 200DMA
20%% of ETFs with positive 1M returns
25%1M and 3M aggregate momentum percentiles
10%Drawdown relief percentile
ValidationRisk Appetite SPY Forward-Return Study buckets the score into equal-count quintiles and tests future SPY returns plus future 6M max drawdown.

Financial Conditions Ease Index

Macro risk-budget overlay built from USD, oil, 5Y yield, 10Y yield, VIX, and MOVE. Higher scores mean easier conditions. Each input is ranked versus its own rolling history and inverted where lower levels are easier.

65%Level Ease: current level percentile versus roughly the prior 3 years, inverted so lower volatility/rates/USD/oil score easier.
35%3M Easing Impulse: 3-month change percentile versus the same input's own history, inverted so falling pressure scores easier.
OverlayVery easy/easy conditions add to risk sleeves; tight/very tight conditions subtract from risk sleeves and raise the cash/quality bar.
Decision UseFCI does not replace breadth or VAMS. It decides how much risk budget to give confirmed signals.

S&P 500 Drawdown Risk Gauge

Downside-underwriting score where higher means higher future S&P 500 drawdown risk. It is separate from risk appetite: markets can be rewarding risk while drawdown risk is also elevated, which argues for smaller adds, better entry discipline, or hedges. The validation target is future max drawdown; forward returns are deliberately excluded because sharp recoveries can obscure the risk question.

30%Breadth Damage: weak 50/200DMA participation, weak 1M breadth, and broad ETF drawdown pressure.
20%Market Pressure: SPY 1M/3M momentum deterioration and drawdown from the 1Y high.
20%Financial Stress: VIX, MOVE, USD, oil, 5Y, and 10Y level/impulse stress percentiles.
15%Leadership Fragility: defensives outperforming cyclicals/growth and cap-weight leadership beating equal weight.
15%Credit / Rates Stress: HY/IG OAS level and impulse plus MOVE/rates pressure when rates-deck FRED cache is available; otherwise HYG/LQD versus SHY is used as the fallback proxy.
BacktestFor each historical score date, future SPY max drawdown is measured over 1M, 3M, 6M, and 12M, along with 5%, 10%, and 15% drawdown hit rates.
Validation StandardHigh-risk deciles should show deeper forward max drawdowns than low-risk deciles. If that relationship fails, the score should be treated as descriptive or redesigned.

Options Intelligence Overlay

Validation-aware pressure layer imported from the Options Intelligence deck. It is intentionally not treated as another price-momentum signal. It asks whether options pressure has historically been helpful or harmful for each symbol, then uses path risk, protection demand, IV pressure, urgent hedge demand, and leadership call chase as sizing discipline.

Options PressurePrimary field is Options Pressure Composite, exported as forward_return_setup_score and repricing_opportunity_score.
Calm Options TapeContext field from low protection demand, call support, gamma stability, and lower vol stress. Calm is not automatically bullish.
Path RiskProtection demand, IV pressure, inverse gamma stability, and put-flow pressure. Higher means rougher near-term path risk.
Protection DemandPut/call demand and downside-protection activity from the options chain.
Urgent Hedge Demand40% put volume/open-interest pressure, 25% put/call volume pressure, 20% average IV percentile, and 15% total volume/open-interest pressure.
Leadership Call ChaseAverage of call demand score and average implied-volatility percentile.
IV PressureAverage IV percentile and ATM-IV proxy percentile; higher means options are expensive versus own history.
ConfidenceBlends validation quality, current-bucket history, sample size, gamma support, path risk, and IV expense.
Constructive UseHigh setup adds risk permission only when PM Action and Forward Return Evidence show add/watch or a stronger historical forward-return bucket.
Risk-Control UseHigh setup with risk-control or worse-return validation subtracts from exposure or raises the bar for entry.
Allocation OverlayThe strategist model converts the current options read into a capped overlay from -4 to +3, then applies smaller multipliers by sleeve.
Master Gauge30% Risk Appetite, 30% Financial Conditions, 25% Drawdown Safety, and 15% Options Intelligence
Important GuardrailA high options score is not automatically bullish when the Options deck validation says high-score regimes have historically been chase risk.

CFTC Positioning Overlay

The CFTC layer has two jobs. Equity-index futures decide whether equity beta is crowded or washed out. Rates/funding futures, including SOFR-3M, are kept as context for the rates deck, FCI, MOVE, duration, and funding-pressure read.

Equity overlayOnly S&P 500, Nasdaq 100, and Russell 2000 futures feed the model's CFTC equity overlay.
SOFR-3MFront-end policy/funding positioning. A crowded short usually means futures positioning leans toward higher implied front-end rates or less easing.
Treasury futuresDuration positioning context for 2Y, 5Y, and 10Y risk, not a direct equity beta signal.
Decision UseUse SOFR/Treasury positioning to tighten or loosen rates/funding interpretation, then confirm with the Rates/Credit page, FCI, MOVE, and spreads.

Optimized Base Weights

The allocation model starts from backtested production base weights, then adjusts them with the weekly signal stack. The optimization used weekly equal-weight ETF group returns, PM-style sleeve constraints, and a Sharpe/Calmar/drawdown objective so the base is diversified rather than simply chasing the highest-return sleeve.

Backtest Window2021 through current price history
Base RoleStrategic starting policy before weekly overlays
Weekly AdjustmentsGroup Strategy Score, z-score overlay, FCI, CFTC positioning, Options Intelligence, VAMS, and regime tilt
Regime GateSelective Only now applies neutral/slight discipline instead of an automatic risk-reduction tilt; Get Defensive and Cut Risk still apply full risk-control tilts.
Final StepWeights are normalized after score and regime tilts

The right side of the table is the forward drawdown test. Low-Risk / High-Risk Avg Max DD compare average future max drawdowns; Extra Avg DD Risk is normalized so positive means high-risk readings led to deeper average drawdowns. Worst Max DD is the deepest observed future drawdown in each bucket. The >5%, >10%, and >15% DD Hit columns show the share of observations that later crossed those drawdown thresholds. Extra 10% Hit Risk is normalized so positive means high-risk readings were followed by more frequent 10% drawdowns.

Regime Decision Framework

Portfolio StateWhat Has To Be TruePM Action
Add Broad Equity RiskIndexes and sectors are both healthy; damage breadth is contained.Own broad beta, reduce cash drag, and add to confirmed leaders.
Own Growth, Do Not Chase The Whole MarketTech/growth is strong, but sector breadth is not broad enough.Keep exposure concentrated in confirmed growth leadership; avoid broad-market overconfidence.
Favor Cyclicals And Economic BetaCyclicals lead, defensives lag, and damage remains controlled.Favor discretionary, financials, industrials, materials, housing, and infrastructure if credit confirms.
Get DefensiveDefensive sectors lead while cyclicals lag.Cut cyclical beta; prefer quality, staples, health care, utilities, real estate, or cash.
Participate, But Keep Quality BiasBroad beta is usable and rates/credit are stable, but breadth is not strong enough for maximum risk.Participate through higher-quality equity, duration, and credit expressions; avoid weak beta chase.
Favor Real Assets / Inflation HedgesCommodity and real-asset groups lead while growth weakens.Shift incremental risk toward energy, materials, metals, commodities, or inflation hedges.
Cut Risk And Wait For RepairDamage breadth is high or fewer ETFs remain in intermediate uptrends.Raise quality, reduce beta, use cash, and wait for breadth repair before adding risk.
Selective OnlySignals are strong in pockets but uneven across the whole map.Use group diagnostics and VAMS confirmation to choose exposures one sleeve at a time.

Credit Risk PremiumHY and IG spreads from the yield-curve deck frame whether credit beta is being paid enough.Tight spread compensation; favor quality over lower-quality beta.
Rates Pressure2Y, 10Y, real yield, breakevens, and curve shape determine the duration/risk-asset discount-rate backdrop.Real-yield pressure matters for equity duration and growth leadership.
Curve / Recession Signal2s10s and 3m10y show whether the curve is steepening, inverted, or normalizing.Use curve shifts as a macro confirmation or warning signal.
Volatility StressMOVE and spread widening flag whether calm credit conditions are breaking.If MOVE rises while spreads remain tight, reduce credit complacency.
Trade TranslationThe yield deck converts rates, credit, curve, and volatility into candidate expressions.Quality credit and duration are the governor on equity beta.

Rates/Credit ConditionEquity Strategy ImplicationPortfolio Translation
Spreads tight + breadth strongRisk-on can continue, but forward compensation is less forgiving.Participate through quality leadership, avoid weak-credit beta chase.
Spreads widening + breadth deterioratingEquity signal is being invalidated by credit stress.Cut beta, raise quality, increase cash/duration ballast.
Yields falling + defensives leadingCould be duration relief or growth scare; breadth decides which.Check whether cyclicals confirm before adding broad beta.
Real yields rising + growth extendedHigher discount-rate pressure can hit long-duration equity leadership.Keep tech/growth exposure selective and watch breadth divergence.

Actionable Positioning Playbook

SetupSignalAction
Crowded long + price/breadth confirmationHigh positioning percentile, positive 13W price, and supportive breadth.Maintain exposure, but add only on clean pullbacks or fresh breadth expansion.
Crowded long + positioning fadingPrice rises while institutional/HF positioning rolls over.Treat as narrowing sponsorship; reduce chase risk and watch for reversal.
Crowded short + price stabilizationLow positioning percentile while price and/or breadth stop deteriorating.Add to repair watchlist; squeeze risk can be favorable if macro backdrop confirms.
SOFR-3M crowded shortLow institutional/HF percentile in SOFR futures with weak front-end futures price action.Treat as front-end funding or hawkish-policy pressure. It informs rates/FCI/MOVE risk control, but it does not directly change the equity CFTC overlay.
Large WoW positioning addOne-week institutional/HF flow is one of the largest in the table.Check whether this is confirmation of a trend or late crowding into an extended move.
Large WoW positioning cutOne-week institutional/HF selling is concentrated in an asset.Use as a risk warning when price is also weak; use as contrarian fuel only if price holds.

Rates / Funding Positioning Lens

SOFR-3M and Treasury futures are treated separately from equity-index futures. They help interpret policy-rate, funding, duration, MOVE, and financial-conditions pressure. They do not directly drive the equity CFTC overlay, which remains based on S&P 500, Nasdaq 100, and Russell 2000 futures.

AssetRoleCurrent ReadPM Translation
SOFR-3MFront-end policy / fundingCrowded Short; percentile 1.9%; 13W price -0.4%; 13W Inst/HF -2.5MCrowded short SOFR futures point to positioning for higher implied front-end rates or less easing; treat as a rates-vol/funding-pressure check, not an equity-beta overlay.
2-Year Treasury NotesTreasury durationCrowded Long; percentile 91.7%; 13W price -0.8%; 13W Inst/HF -80.7KDuration is crowded long; avoid assuming further rate relief without price confirmation and credit stability.
5-Year Treasury NotesTreasury durationCrowded Long; percentile 98.1%; 13W price -1.8%; 13W Inst/HF 328.6KDuration is crowded long; avoid assuming further rate relief without price confirmation and credit stability.
10-Year Treasury NotesTreasury durationCrowded Long; percentile 98.7%; 13W price -2.3%; 13W Inst/HF 229.5KDuration is crowded long; avoid assuming further rate relief without price confirmation and credit stability.

Options Driver Definitions

All component scores are 0-100 reads from the Options Intelligence deck. Higher is not always bullish. The primary allocation score is Options Pressure Composite; PM Action, Validation Read, and Forward Return Evidence decide whether that pressure has historically been favorable, unfavorable, contrarian, or only context for each symbol.

MetricHow It Is CalculatedPM Use
Options Pressure CompositePrimary field from the Options deck, exported as forward_return_setup_score and repricing_opportunity_score. It blends near-term path risk, IV pressure, urgent hedge demand, protection demand, and low calm tape.Higher means option-market pressure is present, not automatically bullish. Use PM Action plus Forward Return Evidence to see whether this ticker's current bucket historically rewarded add/watch or required risk control.
Calm Options TapeContext score from inverse protection demand, call demand, gamma stability, and inverse volatility stress.A quiet tape is not automatically bullish. Treat it as context unless price, breadth, VAMS, and validation agree.
Near-Term Path Risk40% protection demand, 25% volatility stress, 25% inverse gamma stability, and 10% put volume/open-interest pressure.Higher means the path can be rougher now. It is a sizing/timing warning, not a standalone sell signal.
Protection DemandPercentile-style read of put/call demand and protection activity from the options chain.Higher means investors are paying up for downside protection.
Urgent Hedge Demand40% put volume/open-interest pressure, 25% put/call volume pressure, 20% average IV percentile, and 15% total volume/open-interest pressure.Higher means protection demand is shorter-fuse and more urgent.
Gamma Stability0-100 gamma-stability proxy from the options surface and open-interest model.Higher can mean more stabilizing options structure; lower can leave price more exposed to air pockets.
Leadership Call ChaseAverage of call demand score and average implied-volatility percentile.Higher says upside demand may be crowded or expensive. This can be bullish confirmation or a do-not-chase warning depending on validation.
IV PressureAverage of each symbol's average implied-volatility percentile and 30D ATM-IV proxy percentile.Higher means options are more expensive versus their own history; it can validate stress, expensive upside demand, or a contrarian setup depending on PM Action.
Macro-Options TransmissionMacro-sensitive options pressure from HYG, LQD, TLT, IEF, KRE, and XLF.Shows whether macro stress is entering credit, duration, and financial-sector risk-transfer markets.
Pressure ConfirmationAverage of near-term path risk, IV pressure, urgent hedge demand, and protection demand.Confirms whether raw options pressure is broad enough to matter for sizing discipline.
ConfidenceBlend of validation quality, current-bucket history, sample size, gamma support, path risk, and IV expense from the Options deck.Higher means the PM action/validated signal should carry more weight; lower means defer more to breadth, VAMS, macro, and price.

Model Allocation

A signal-driven model allocation based on optimized base weights, group scores, regime, financial-conditions risk budget, CFTC equity-crowding overlay, Options Intelligence risk-transfer overlay, and the full VAMS buy/sell universe plus fresh flip momentum overlay. It is a strategy translation layer, not a position-sizing recommendation. Price/breadth as of 2026-07-17; breadth metrics as of 2026-07-17; CFTC positioning as of 2026-07-14; VAMS as of 2026-07-22; Options as of 2026-07-16.

Interpretation: Base Weight is the backtested production anchor. Signal is the base group score after breadth, price returns, trend, damage, and ETF-deck z-score extension/repair overlay. Positioning, VAMS, FCI, and Options overlays adjust the signal where each input is relevant to the sleeve. Adjusted Signal drives Score Tilt; Regime Tilt then applies the current top-down regime before final model weights are normalized. View is now based on final Model Weight versus Base Weight using a 0.75 percentage-point materiality band, so the label reconciles with the displayed allocation. The sleeves are intentionally broad enough to frame a portfolio, but detailed enough that style, factor, thematic, sector, industry, international, rates/credit, metals, commodities, and cash decisions do not collapse into the same repeated message.
